news.text: 5 January saw American pop icon and Republican congressman **Sonny Bono** die at the age of 62 after colliding with a tree while skiing in Lake Tahoe. Rising to international fame alongside former wife Cher with 1960s anthems like *I Got You Babe*, Bono had pulled off the remarkably improbable transition from bell-bottomed pop star to respected Capitol Hill politician. Fellow politicians praised his self-deprecating wit, admitting they had rarely met a legislator who took his work so seriously and his own ego so lightly.

18 January saw **"Stone Cold" Steve Austin** win the 30-man Royal Rumble match in San Jose, California, punching his ticket to the main event of *WrestleMania XIV*. Austin last eliminated rising rival The Rock, while Mick Foley set a bizarre longevity record by entering the match three separate times under his various personas of Cactus Jack, Chainsaw Charlie and Mankind. Up in a private luxury box, suspended heavyweight boxer **Mike Tyson** applauded the mayhem, setting the stage for an explosive pop-culture crossover.

news.text: 21 January saw Capcom unleash survival horror landmark *Resident Evil 2* on the **Sony PlayStation** in North America, establishing a new high watermark for digital dread. Introducing rookie police officer Leon S. Kennedy and college student Claire Redfield amid the catastrophic destruction of **Raccoon City**, the game employed two discs and a clever zapping system that let players experience interlocking perspectives. Gamers quickly forgave the awkward tank controls in exchange for the sheer thrill of running out of shotgun shells in dark corridors.

23 January saw James Cameron's cinematic juggernaut *Titanic* dock in British cinemas, unleashing unprecedented queues at multiplex box offices nationwide. Starring **Leonardo DiCaprio** and **Kate Winslet** as star-crossed lovers aboard the doomed luxury liner, the three-hour disaster romance silenced critics who had predicted an expensive box office catastrophe. Instead, audiences flocked back for repeated viewings, leaving cinema aisles littered with soggy tissues and ushering in an era of unavoidable Celine Dion ballads.

24 January saw Britpop titans **Oasis** climb to number one on the UK singles chart with *All Around the World*. Clocking in at an indulgent nine minutes and thirty-eight seconds, the sprawling orchestral epic set an enduring Guinness World Record as the longest single ever to top the British charts. Noel Gallagher unapologetically loaded the track with dozens of guitar overdubs and repeated key changes, apparently operating on the logic that more of everything was invariably better.

news.text: 26 January saw US President **Bill Clinton** forcefully deny allegations of an extramarital affair with former White House intern Monica Lewinsky during a televised press conference. Wagging his index finger firmly toward reporters, Clinton famously declared that he did not have sexual relations with that woman. Political analysts marvelled at the sheer bravado of the performance, oblivious to the fact that linguistic gymnastics over the definition of the word "is" would soon dominate global news headlines for months.

news.text: 28 January saw the automotive world abuzz as American giant **Ford** moved closer to acquiring the passenger car division of Sweden's **Volvo** in an eye-watering $6.45 billion deal. The transaction sought to combine Ford's global manufacturing muscle with the Swedish marque's unimpeachable reputation for boxy styling and uncompromising passenger safety. Motorists wondered whether future Swedish estates might trade their traditional Scandinavian sturdiness for Detroit-style cup holders.
